title: NIST SP 800-190 — Application Container Security Guide

controls.title: Image vulnerabilities — scan images for known CVEs
controls.statement: Images should be scanned for vulnerabilities and vulnerable images should not be deployed.
controls.expected: no known vulnerabilities above the accepted threshold
controls.remediation: Rebuild from a patched base image or upgrade the affected packages; gate deployment on the scan result.

controls.title: Image configuration defects — non-root, no baked secrets, healthcheck
controls.statement: Images should be built with secure configuration: run as non-root, contain no embedded secrets, and declare a healthcheck.
controls.remediation: Add a non-root USER to the final stage of the image.

controls.title: Embedded clear-text secrets in images
controls.statement: Secrets must not be stored within images; they should be delivered at runtime from a secrets manager.
controls.expected: no clear-text credentials found in image layers or config
controls.remediation: Remove the secret, rotate it, and inject secrets at runtime via a secrets manager or BuildKit secret mount.

controls.title: Use of untrusted images — malware and known-bad content
controls.statement: Only trusted images should be used; images should be scanned for malware and known-bad binaries.
controls.expected: no cryptominer / web-shell / known-bad binaries present in any layer
controls.remediation: Rebuild from a trusted base; investigate provenance and rotate any exposed credentials.

controls.title: Software bill of materials — image inventory
controls.statement: Organizations should maintain an inventory of the software contained in each image.
controls.expected: an SBOM was generated for the image
controls.remediation: Generate and retain an SBOM for every image as a mandatory build step.

controls.title: Image license governance
controls.statement: Image components should be reviewed for license obligations that conflict with distribution.
controls.expected: no components carry a disallowed license
controls.remediation: Replace disallowed-license components or record a reviewed waiver.

controls.title: Registry — insecure connections and untrusted sources
controls.statement: Connections to registries should be secure and images should be pulled only from trusted registries by immutable digest.
controls.expected: images are pinned by immutable digest, not a mutable tag
controls.remediation: Pin images by sha256 digest and restrict pulls to an allowlist of trusted registries.

controls.title: Orchestrator — unbounded administrative access (RBAC least privilege)
controls.statement: Access to the orchestrator should be least-privilege; over-permissioned identities are a primary escalation path.
controls.expected: no subject holds cluster-admin / wildcard / escalate-class permissions unnecessarily
controls.remediation: Scope Roles to the exact verbs and resources needed; remove wildcard and escalate/bind/impersonate grants.

controls.title: Container runtime — insecure configuration and isolation
controls.statement: Containers should run with least privilege: no privileged mode, dropped capabilities, read-only root filesystem, and a seccomp profile.
controls.expected: container is not privileged and drops unnecessary capabilities
controls.remediation: Drop ALL capabilities and add back only those required; disable privileged mode; apply seccomp RuntimeDefault.

controls.title: Container runtime — unbounded network access from containers
controls.statement: Egress from containers should be restricted to only the destinations required.
controls.expected: a default-deny egress posture with an explicit allowlist
controls.remediation: Apply a default-deny egress NetworkPolicy and allowlist only required destinations.

controls.title: Host OS — large attack surface / shared kernel
controls.statement: Container host operating systems should be hardened and their attack surface minimized per the CIS Docker host benchmark.
controls.expected: host and daemon configuration pass the CIS Docker host controls
controls.remediation: Apply the CIS Docker host and daemon hardening controls; run the daemon rootless where possible.
